name: rematch2
resume: CRAN rematch2 2.1.2 is inventoried. All 8 exports are checked. Matching uses Python's re module, and the tables use the tibble columns already translated. There is no crate.

functions.name: $.rematch_allrecords
functions.done: Reads match, start, or end from each all-match record. Each entry is a vector.

check.case: all first-name records from two notable strings

proof.r:
suppressPackageStartupMessages(library(rematch2))
pos <- re_exec_all(c("  Ben Franklin and Jefferson Davis", "\tMillard Fillmore"), "(?<first>[[:upper:]][[:lower:]]+) (?<last>[[:upper:]][[:lower:]]+)")
        one <- function() {
          paste(vapply(`$.rematch_allrecords`(pos$first, "match"), paste, "", collapse = "+"), collapse = ",")
        }
        ans <- one()
        elapsed <- numeric(20)
        for (i in seq_len(20)) {
          t0 <- as.numeric(Sys.time())
          one()
          elapsed[[i]] <- as.numeric(Sys.time()) - t0
        }
        cat(ans, "\n", sep = "")
        cat(sprintf("%.17g\n", median(elapsed) * 1000))
proof.python:
import statistics
import time

from rematch2 import dollar_rematch_allrecords, re_exec_all
pos = re_exec_all(["  Ben Franklin and Jefferson Davis", "\tMillard Fillmore"], "(?<first>[[:upper:]][[:lower:]]+) (?<last>[[:upper:]][[:lower:]]+)")
def one():
    return ",".join("+".join(row) for row in dollar_rematch_allrecords(pos["first"], "match"))

ans = one()
elapsed = []
for _ in range(20):
    started = time.perf_counter()
    one()
    elapsed.append((time.perf_counter() - started) * 1000)
print(ans)
print(f"{statistics.median(elapsed):.17g}")

functions.name: bind_re_match
functions.done: Runs re_match on a column and attaches the new columns. The R argument from is column, because from is a Python keyword.

check.case: two car names, make and model groups

proof.r:
suppressPackageStartupMessages(library(rematch2))
cars <- data.frame(rowname = c("Mazda RX4", "Datsun 710"), mpg = c(21, 22.8), stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
        one <- function() {
          paste(bind_re_match_(cars, "rowname", "^(?<make>\\w+) ?(?<model>.+)?$")$make, bind_re_match_(cars, "rowname", "^(?<make>\\w+) ?(?<model>.+)?$")$model, sep = "=", collapse = ",")
        }
        ans <- one()
        elapsed <- numeric(20)
        for (i in seq_len(20)) {
          t0 <- as.numeric(Sys.time())
          one()
          elapsed[[i]] <- as.numeric(Sys.time()) - t0
        }
        cat(ans, "\n", sep = "")
        cat(sprintf("%.17g\n", median(elapsed) * 1000))

import statistics
import time

from rematch2 import bind_re_match
from tibble import tibble
cars = tibble(rowname=["Mazda RX4", "Datsun 710"], mpg=[21.0, 22.8])
pattern = r"^(?<make>\w+) ?(?<model>.+)?$"
def one():
    return ",".join(f"{m}={d}" for m, d in zip(bind_re_match(cars, "rowname", pattern)["make"], bind_re_match(cars, "rowname", pattern)["model"]))

ans = one()
elapsed = []
for _ in range(20):
    started = time.perf_counter()
    one()
    elapsed.append((time.perf_counter() - started) * 1000)
print(ans)
print(f"{statistics.median(elapsed):.17g}")

functions.name: bind_re_match_
functions.done: The same attachment as bind_re_match. R's quoting of from is unnecessary in Python, so both take the column name as a string.

functions.name: re_exec
functions.done: Returns the first match with 1-based start and end. A missed group is an empty string at position 0.

check.case: two notable-name strings, first match positions

proof.r:
suppressPackageStartupMessages(library(rematch2))
notes <- c("  Ben Franklin and Jefferson Davis", "\tMillard Fillmore")
pattern <- "(?<first>[[:upper:]][[:lower:]]+) (?<last>[[:upper:]][[:lower:]]+)"
        one <- function() {
          pos <- re_exec(notes, pattern)
paste(pos$first$match, pos$first$start, pos$first$end, sep = ":", collapse = ",")
        }
        ans <- one()
        elapsed <- numeric(20)
        for (i in seq_len(20)) {
          t0 <- as.numeric(Sys.time())
          one()
          elapsed[[i]] <- as.numeric(Sys.time()) - t0
        }
        cat(ans, "\n", sep = "")
        cat(sprintf("%.17g\n", median(elapsed) * 1000))

functions.name: re_match
functions.done: Returns the first match and each named capture. Python's re compiles the pattern after rewriting PCRE names.

check.case: seven date strings and a named ISO pattern

proof.r:
suppressPackageStartupMessages(library(rematch2))
dates <- c("2016-04-20", "1977-08-08", "not a date", "2016", "76-03-02", "2012-06-30", "2015-01-21 19:58")
pattern <- "(?<year>[0-9]{4})-(?<month>[0-1][0-9])-(?<day>[0-3][0-9])"
        one <- function() {
          paste(ifelse(is.na(one_value <- re_match(dates, pattern)$year), "NA", one_value), collapse = ",")
        }
        ans <- one()
        elapsed <- numeric(20)
        for (i in seq_len(20)) {
          t0 <- as.numeric(Sys.time())
          one()
          elapsed[[i]] <- as.numeric(Sys.time()) - t0
        }
        cat(ans, "\n", sep = "")
        cat(sprintf("%.17g\n", median(elapsed) * 1000))

import statistics
import time

from rematch2 import re_match
dates = ["2016-04-20", "1977-08-08", "not a date", "2016", "76-03-02", "2012-06-30", "2015-01-21 19:58"]
pattern = "(?<year>[0-9]{4})-(?<month>[0-1][0-9])-(?<day>[0-3][0-9])"
def one():
    return ",".join("NA" if v is None else v for v in re_match(dates, pattern)["year"])

ans = one()
elapsed = []
for _ in range(20):
    started = time.perf_counter()
    one()
    elapsed.append((time.perf_counter() - started) * 1000)
print(ans)
print(f"{statistics.median(elapsed):.17g}")
